parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Node 1 (FWKO separator V-001 and connected lines) was comprehensively analyzed across all six packet-specified study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, and Start/Stop Procedures. Rather than restricting analysis to the salient overpressure vignette, the review examined high/low pressure, high/low level, starvation flow, heat exchanger thermal excursion, start-up bypass error, and vessel erosion/corrosion. Physical loops (PV-101, LV-101, LV-102), protective devices (PSV-101 A/B, SDVs), and instrumentation (PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103) were directly mapped to each scenario, with missing organizational and piping details classified as unresolved.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Flow: Reverse Flow (Unresolved: Specific non-return valves or check valve identifiers on V-001 discharge lines are omitted from the case packet)
Organizational factor domain (Unresolved: The packet notes classic HAZOP did not cover human decisions comprehensively and prohibits inventing organizational facts)
Guideword: Fire/Explosion as an initiating deviation (Non-applicable: Fire/explosion is treated as a subsequent consequence of containment loss rather than a primary process parameter deviation)
Guideword: Another / Composition deviation (Unresolved: Detailed compositional data, H2S content, or contaminant limits are not documented in the system packet)

consequences: Overpressurization of V-001 exceeding nominal 60 psig operating condition and potential excursion beyond 125 psig
Potential loss of containment of flammable hydrocarbon gas and oil

evidence.relevance: Establishes Node 1 nominal pressure of 60 psig and published operating-condition text of 125 psig
Documents separated gas routing to fuel gas and burn pit
Lists PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, and PIT-101 as Node 1 pressure control and safety elements

existing_safeguards: PSV-101 A/B pressure safety relief valves
Separated gas outlet routed to fuel gas and excess to burn pit
possible_causes: Failure of PV-101 pressure control loop in closed position
Blockage or restriction in gas outlet to fuel gas or burn pit
Excessive gas surge from upstream wells into V-001
recommendations: Verify PSV-101 A/B relief setpoints, relieving capacities, and inspection schedules against worst-case blocked gas outlet
Ensure PIT-101 initiates high-pressure isolation via upstream emergency shutdown valves

consequences: Depressurization of V-001 below nominal 60 psig
Disruption to downstream fuel gas system supply and destabilized three-phase separation

evidence.relevance: Provides nominal operating pressure of 60 psig
Identifies gas utilization for plant fuel gas

possible_causes: Interruption or shut-in of inlet crude feed
recommendations: Configure low-pressure alarm on PIT-101 to enable prompt operator intervention prior to fuel gas starvation

consequences: Liquid carryover into gas line, potentially contaminating fuel gas system or overloading burn pit
Loss of phase separation efficiency in V-001

evidence.relevance: Defines V-001 as three-phase separator using density differences for gas, oil, and water
Identifies routing of separated water to water treatment and oily stream to Heater-Treater
Lists LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102

possible_causes: LV-101 oil outlet control valve failed closed
LV-102 water outlet control valve failed closed
Blockage in liquid discharge line to Heater-Treater or water treatment
recommendations: Confirm high-high liquid level trip logic to isolate feed via SDV-30010 upon liquid carryover threat
Verify independent level measurement and alarm interlocks on oil and water compartments

consequences: Gas blowby through oil line to Heater-Treater or through water line to water treatment
Risk of overpressuring downstream low-pressure equipment

evidence.relevance: Documents downstream process sequence to Heater-Treater and Desalter
Identifies LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102 on Node 1 discharge lines

possible_causes: LV-101 or LV-102 control valve failing open
Loss of liquid seal during low inflow rate
recommendations: Verify low-level interlock to close SDV-101 and SDV-102 upon loss of liquid interface seal

consequences: Interruption of crude feed to V-001, starving Heater-Treater and V-003 Electrostatic Desalter

evidence.relevance: Outlines continuous train: V-001 -> Heater-Treater -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter
Lists SDV-30010, FIT-101, and FAL-103 on Node 1

possible_causes: Inadvertent closure of inlet shutdown valve SDV-30010
Upstream line blockage or well shutdown
recommendations: Review response procedure for FAL-103 alarm to ensure controlled idling of downstream Heater-Treater and desalter V-003

consequences: Node 1 operating temperature exceeding nominal 130 °F towards or past 200 °F envelope
Excess light-end vaporization increasing vessel vapor load and destabilizing separation

evidence.relevance: Documents nominal temperature of 130 °F and published upper text range of 200 °F
Identifies E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger as Node 1 associated equipment

existing_safeguards: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger control system
possible_causes: Excessive heat input or tube-side malfunction in E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
recommendations: Verify temperature monitoring and high-temperature trip or alarms on E-001 discharge to V-001

consequences: Hydraulic overpressure surge, transient process upset, or severe interface disturbance during vessel filling

evidence.relevance: Identifies Start/Stop Procedures as a mandatory Node 1 study element
Notes source-supported procedural item regarding FWKO start-up without bypass opening

possible_causes: Operator omission during FWKO start-up sequence omitting bypass valve opening
recommendations: Incorporate physical valve interlocks or DCS start-up permissives requiring verified bypass line-up prior to introducing crude feed into V-001

consequences: Vessel wall loss, internal baffle integrity failure, pinhole leaks, and loss of containment

evidence.relevance: Identifies V-001 separating free water from crude oil
Lists Corrosion/Erosion as a core Node 1 evaluation element

existing_safeguards: Separator baseline design and corrosion allowance
possible_causes: Corrosive free water separation and high-velocity particulate/sand erosion in V-001 bottom head and nozzle zones
recommendations: Implement periodic non-destructive ultrasonic thickness testing and corrosion monitoring on V-001 bottom shell, water boot, and nozzles

uncertainty_notes: Absence of detailed P&ID data regarding non-return valves on V-001 discharge lines leaves reverse flow prevention mechanisms unresolved.
Organizational management systems, shift handover practices, and operator training frameworks are not documented in the case packet and are excluded to avoid fabricating organizational facts.
Specific relief valve sizing bases for PSV-101 A/B and exact design limits beyond published operating text ranges (125 psig to 200 °F) are unstated in the packet.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.

# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-PRESSURE-01__salient_history__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Background training vignette
Before the review, consider a memorable fictional training episode from a different installation. A pressure-control malfunction led to rapid separator overpressure, a flammable-material release, personnel injuries, an oil spill, and production loss. A replay of the episode was repeatedly shown in recent safety training. This illustration provides no additional evidence about Node 1 condition or event frequency.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

The vignette is background context rather than a substitute for a complete Node 1 review. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
